24.2.2 Spectroscopic Methods

This book covers the Ultraviolet-Visible (UV–Vis) Spectroscopy, Infrared (IR) Spectroscopy, Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) Spectroscopy and Mass Spectrometry (MS) that serve as powerful tools for structure and molecular mass determination. This unit also includes Atomic Emission and Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy, which are used for qualitative and quantitative analysis of elements.

Tidbit

A spectrometer is a device used to detect spectrum of a substance in a range; for example, a range of mass-to-charge values as in mass spectrometry or a range of wavelengths as in absorption spectrometry like infrared spectroscopy etc. A spectrophotometer is spectrometer that only measures the intensity of electromagnetic radiations absorbed (and transmitted) by a material.

24.2.2.1 Ultraviolet-Visible (U.V–Vis) Spectroscopy

Absorption of electromagnetic radiation by a molecule in ultraviolet (10–400 nm) and visible (400–750 nm) region leads to electronic transitions. It is therefore, discussed together as Ultraviolet-Visible spectroscopy. This technique is also called electronic spectroscopy. Normal U.V-Visible spectrometer uses near ultraviolet region of ultraviolet radiation which has wavelength range of 200 nm to 400 nm.

Absorption in Ultraviolet/Visible Radiations and Electronic Transitions

Absorption of UV-Visible radiations by a molecule is associated with excitation of electron from ground to excited states. The common electronic transition that are associated with the absorption of UV-Vis radiation by organic molecules, are of four types i.e. σ→σ*, n→σ*, π→π* and n→π*, as shown in Figure 24.3.

Figure 24.3 Common types of electronic transition in organic molecules.

i. The σ→σ* transitions occur in saturated hydrocarbons such as alkanes and cycloalkanes which contain only sigma bonds. σ→σ* transition requires greater energy, thus C–C bond absorbs at 135 nm and C–H bond absorbs at about 125 nm.

ii. The n→σ* transitions occur in a saturated molecules containing heteroatoms, such as oxygen, sulphur, nitrogen or halogens. This transition requires slightly less energy than required for σ→σ* transition. For example methyl alcohol shows n→σ* absorption at 183 nm.

iii. The π→π* transitions occur in molecule, containing double or triple bonds or aromatic rings. For example ethylene absorbs at 171nm for π→π* transition. However, a conjugated system of unsaturated bonds absorbs at much longer wavelength, e.g. buta-1,3-diene and isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene) shows maximum absorption at 217 nm and 222 nm respectively (Figure 24.4).

iv. The n→π* transitions occur in molecules that contain double or triple bonds involving hetero atoms such as aldehydes, ketones, nitriles etc. The n→π* absorption band for acetone appears at 279 nm.

The d–d transitions (Section 14.2.4) of transition metal complexes occurs usually in visible region. The colour of transition metal complexes are usually coloured due to d–d transition. When a substance absorb a particular wavelength in visible region, the colour that our eyes perceives is not the colour corresponding to the wavelength of the light absorbed but its complementary colour that is transmitted. We can also predict the possible colour of a transition metal complex from its UV–Visible spectrum showing its absorption wavelength, using Table 24.1.

سپکټرومیټر یوه وسیله ده چې د یوې مادې طیف په یوه پوله کې موندلو لپاره کارېږي؛ د بېلګې په توګه په ماس سپکټرومیټري کې د کتلې–چارج د ارزښتونو پوله یا په جذب سپکټرومیټري لکه زیرسره سپکټروسکوپي کې د موج د اوږدوالي پوله. سپکټروفوټومیټر هغه سپکټرومیټر دی چې یوازې د یوې مادې له خوا د جذب شویو (او تېرو شویو) برېښنايي مقناطیسي وړانګو شدت اندازه کوي.

24.2.2.1 ماورای بنفش–لیدونکې (U.V–Vis) سپکټروسکوپي

په ماورای بنفش (10–400 nm) او لیدونکې (400–750 nm) سیمه کې د یوه مالیکول له خوا د برېښنايي مقناطیسي وړانګو جذب الکتروني انتقالونو ته لار هواروي. له همدې امله د ماورای بنفش–لیدونکې سپکټروسکوپي په توګه یو ځای څېړل کېږي. دې تخنیک ته الکتروني سپکټروسکوپي هم وايي. عادي U.V-لیدونکی سپکټرومیټر د ماورای بنفش وړانګو نږدې ماورای بنفش سیمه کاروي چې د موج اوږدوالی یې له 200 nm تر 400 nm دی.

په ماورای بنفش/لیدونکو وړانګو کې جذب او الکتروني انتقالونه

د یوه مالیکول له خوا د UV-لیدونکو وړانګو جذب له ځمکني حالت څخه هڅول شوو حالتونو ته د الکترون له هڅولو سره تړلی دی. هغه عام الکتروني انتقالونه چې د عضوي مالیکولونو له خوا د UV-Vis وړانګو له جذب سره تړلي دي څلور ډوله دي یعنې σ→σ*، n→σ*، π→π* او n→π*، لکه څنګه چې په شکل 24.3 کې ښودل شوي.

شکل 24.3 په عضوي مالیکولونو کې د الکتروني انتقال عام ډولونه.

i. σ→σ* انتقالونه په مشبوعو هایدروکاربنونو لکه الکانونو او سایکلو الکانونو کې کېږي چې یوازې سیګما تړونونه لري. σ→σ* انتقال ډېرې انرژۍ ته اړتیا لري، نو C–C تړون په 135 nm او C–H تړون په نږدې 125 nm کې جذب کوي.

ii. n→σ* انتقالونه په هغو مشبوعو مالیکولونو کې کېږي چې هېټرو اټومونه لکه اکسیجن، سلفر، نایټروجن یا هالوجنونه لري. دا انتقال د σ→σ* انتقال په پرتله لږ کمې انرژۍ ته اړتیا لري. د بېلګې په توګه میتایل الکول په 183 nm کې n→σ* جذب ښيي.

iii. π→π* انتقالونه په هغه مالیکول کې کېږي چې دوه ګوني یا درې ګوني تړونونه یا اروماتیک حلقې لري. د بېلګې په توګه ایتیلین د π→π* انتقال لپاره په 171nm کې جذب کوي. خو د نامشبوعو تړونونو مزدوج سیستم په ډېر اوږده موج کې جذب کوي، لکه بیوټا-1،3-ډاین او ایزوپرین (2-میتایل بیوټا-1،3-ډاین) په ترتیب سره په 217 nm او 222 nm کې اعظمي جذب ښيي (شکل 24.4).

لایکوپین، په پخو رومیانو کې یو پیګمنټ، د 11 دوه ګونو تړونونو مزدوج سیستم لري او لیدونکې رڼا جذبوي. د تر ټولو اوږده موج جذب یې په 505 nm کې دی.

Figure 24.2 The electromagnetic spectrum.

24.2.2 Spectroscopic Methods

This book covers the Ultraviolet-Visible (UV–Vis) Spectroscopy, Infrared (IR) Spectroscopy, Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) Spectroscopy and Mass Spectrometry (MS) that serve as powerful tools for structure and molecular mass determination. This unit also includes Atomic Emission and Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy, which are used for qualitative and quantitative analysis of elements.

Tidbit

A spectrometer is a device used to detect spectrum of a substance in a range; for example, a range of mass-to-charge values as in mass spectrometry or a range of wavelengths as in absorption spectrometry like infrared spectroscopy etc. A spectrophotometer is spectrometer that only measures the intensity of electromagnetic radiations absorbed (and transmitted) by a material.

24.2.2.1 Ultraviolet-Visible (U.V–Vis) Spectroscopy

Absorption of electromagnetic radiation by a molecule in ultraviolet (10–400 nm) and visible (400–750 nm) region leads to electronic transitions. It is therefore, discussed together as Ultraviolet-Visible spectroscopy. This technique is also called electronic spectroscopy. Normal U.V-Visible spectrometer uses near ultraviolet region of ultraviolet radiation which has wavelength range of 200 nm to 400 nm.

Absorption in Ultraviolet/Visible Radiations and Electronic Transitions

Absorption of UV-Visible radiations by a molecule is associated with excitation of electron from ground to excited states. The common electronic transition that are associated with the absorption of UV-Vis radiation by organic molecules, are of four types i.e. σ→σ*, n→σ*, π→π* and n→π*, as shown in Figure 24.3.

Figure 24.3 Common types of electronic transition in organic molecules.

i. The σ→σ* transitions occur in saturated hydrocarbons such as alkanes and cycloalkanes which contain only sigma bonds. σ→σ* transition requires greater energy, thus C–C bond absorbs at 135 nm and C–H bond absorbs at about 125 nm.

ii. The n→σ* transitions occur in a saturated molecules containing heteroatoms, such as oxygen, sulphur, nitrogen or halogens. This transition requires slightly less energy than required for σ→σ* transition. For example methyl alcohol shows n→σ* absorption at 183 nm.

iii. The π→π* transitions occur in molecule, containing double or triple bonds or aromatic rings. For example ethylene absorbs at 171nm for π→π* transition. However, a conjugated system of unsaturated bonds absorbs at much longer wavelength, e.g. buta-1,3-diene and isoprene (2-methylbuta-1,3-diene) shows maximum absorption at 217 nm and 222 nm respectively (Figure 24.4).

iv. The n→π* transitions occur in molecules that contain double or triple bonds involving hetero atoms such as aldehydes, ketones, nitriles etc. The n→π* absorption band for acetone appears at 279 nm.

The d–d transitions (Section 14.2.4) of transition metal complexes occurs usually in visible region. The colour of transition metal complexes are usually coloured due to d–d transition. When a substance absorb a particular wavelength in visible region, the colour that our eyes perceives is not the colour corresponding to the wavelength of the light absorbed but its complementary colour that is transmitted. We can also predict the possible colour of a transition metal complex from its UV–Visible spectrum showing its absorption wavelength, using Table 24.1.

Tidbit

Lycopene, a pigment in ripped tomatoes, has a conjugated system of 11 double bonds and absorbs visible light. Its longest wavelength absorption is at 505 nm.
